title: How Much Text Is Too Much on a Slide? (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: How Much Text Is Too Much?
slides.notes: A slide fills with words, you stop listening to read, and you fall behind on both. Here's how to spot an overloaded slide and fix it.

slides.title: Text-heavy slides split attention
bullets: In video, the slide runs out of time
slides.notes: When everything is written down, nothing looks important. And in a video, the slide only stays up while the narration runs, so viewers pause or give up.

slides.title: Five quick tests for overload
bullets: Headline makes a point, not a label
slides.notes: Glance for three seconds, then look away. Can you say what it was about? If you could read the slide aloud as your script, move that text.

slides.title: Move extra text where it helps
slides.notes: The words you cut don't disappear. Explanations go into the speaker notes, reference detail goes in a handout, and one crowded slide often becomes two or three clear ones.

slides.title: Before and after: the leave policy
bullets: Before: "Leave policy" and five dense bullets
After: "Request leave two weeks ahead, through the HR portal"
Three steps: submit, manager reviews, reply
Detail moves to the speaker notes
slides.notes: The headline now makes the point, a simple graphic shows the steps, and the narration carries the detail about accrual and reply times.

slides.title: Lighter slides make better videos
slides.notes: The slide shows the point; your voice explains it. On Pro, a.i. directs the video, landing each key point on its word. Start with Basic at powerpoint2vid.com.
